title: Low-dose Imaging Using Single-electron Detection with an Integration-type SOI Pixel Detector in Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Direct electron detectors (DEDs) are essential instruments for low-dose and high-resolution observations in transmission electron microscopy (TEM), such as biological specimens [1] and materials that are sensitive to electron-beam irradiation [2]. The typical DEDs are monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS) and hybrid pixel detectors. In MAPS, the sensitive region and the complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) circuit are built up on the same substrate. We can obtain sharp images with a small pixel size because we can make the detector thinner to prevent incident electrons from scattering in the lateral direction. In the hybrid type, the sensor and CMOS circuit are manufactured individually. Then, they are connected with metal bumps. The secondary charge generated by incident electrons can be collected efficiently because a bias voltage can be applied to the sensor. Recently, silicon-on-insulator (SOI) pixel detectors [3], which are monolithic radiation detectors, have been applied as DEDs in a 30-kV transmission electron microscope [4]. In this study, we show that imaging using single-electron detection can be realized with an SOI pixel detector designed for X-ray detection as a DED in a conventional transmission electron microscope.
